source_pages.title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview

questions.question: A law firm wants DLP to catch a partner emailing 95 social security numbers to a personal address, but not flag a single SSN in an internal HR email. How does Purview DLP distinguish these cases?
options: DLP uses deep content analysis, not a simple text scan: primary matches, regular expressions, internal function validation, and secondary matches in proximity, so conditions can require a count threshold and context
DLP only counts characters, so both emails are treated identically
DLP cannot inspect email content at all; it only checks sender domains
DLP flags every email containing any number sequence
questions.explanation: Correct: A. DLP uses deep content analysis — primary data matches to keywords, regular expressions, internal function validation, and secondary data matches in proximity — and policy conditions can specify context such as 95 SSNs emailed outside the org. B is wrong — DLP is explicitly not a simple text scan. C is wrong — DLP inspects content in Exchange. D is wrong — thresholds and corroborative evidence prevent flagging every number.
questions.source_quote: DLP uses deep content analysis—not a simple text scan. It analyzes content for primary data matches to keywords, by the evaluation of regular expressions, by internal function validation, and by secondary data matches that are in proximity to the primary data match.

questions.question: A company rolls out a DLP policy blocking external sharing of credit card data, but users complain legitimate workflows broke on day one. What deployment practice should they have followed, and what happens in that mode?
options: Deploy directly in enforce mode, because DLP has no testing mode
Deploy first in simulation mode, where actions defined in a policy aren't applied, then monitor, fine-tune, and only then turn enforcement on
Deploy in audit mode, which blocks sharing but does not log it
Disable the policy for 30 days, because policies take a month to take effect
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Microsoft advises planning policies and deploying them in simulation mode, evaluating impact before running them in more restrictive modes; in simulation mode actions defined in a policy are not applied. A is wrong — simulation mode exists precisely for this. C is wrong — audit/simulate does not block. D is wrong — policies generally take effect about an hour after being turned on, not a month.
questions.source_quote: Evaluate the impact of the controls by implementing them with a DLP policy in simulation mode. Actions defined in a policy aren't applied while the policy is in simulation mode.

questions.question: An employee tries to paste customer health records from a Word document into a personal webmail tab, and separately tries to copy a labeled file to a USB drive. Which DLP location covers each action?
options: Both are covered only by Exchange DLP
Neither is covered; DLP only protects data at rest in SharePoint
The paste into webmail is covered by Office apps / inline web traffic controls, and the USB copy is covered by endpoint DLP on Windows 10/11 and macOS devices
USB copy is covered by Exchange DLP and webmail paste by SharePoint DLP
questions.explanation: Correct: C. DLP covers Office applications and inline web traffic for browser paste scenarios, and endpoint DLP covers devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and the three most recent macOS versions, including restricting copying a sensitive item to a removable USB device. A is wrong — Exchange covers mail flow, not endpoint actions. B is wrong — DLP covers data at rest, in use, and in motion. D swaps the locations.
questions.source_quote: Windows 10, Windows 11, and macOS (three latest released versions) Devices: Audit or restrict copying a sensitive item to a removable USB device.

questions.question: A user sends a Teams channel message containing a credit card number. The DLP policy is configured to block. What does the user experience, and how does this differ from Exchange?
options: Exchange and Teams behave identically in every respect
Teams messages cannot be blocked; DLP only logs them
Teams DLP deletes the entire channel
In Teams chat, the sensitive information won't be displayed / the message is blocked from being shared; in Exchange the message can be blocked with an override and policy tip
questions.explanation: Correct: D. For Teams chat and channel, DLP blocks sensitive information from being shared and the sensitive information is not displayed; for Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive, DLP can block with override via policy tip, block without override, or show a tip. B is wrong — Teams chat and channel messages are a DLP location with blocking. C is wrong — DLP never deletes a channel. A is wrong — Teams has distinct behaviors, e.g. no email notifications for Teams DLP.
questions.source_quote: For Teams chat, the sensitive information won't be displayed.

questions.question: A hospital stores patient files in an on-premises file share and wants DLP to quarantine files containing health records. What is required, and what action can DLP take there?
options: Deploy the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner, after which DLP can move a file from where it is stored to a quarantine folder
Nothing extra; on-premises shares are covered automatically by Exchange policies
Migrate the files to SharePoint first; on-premises repositories cannot be DLP locations
Use endpoint DLP only, which quarantines files on the file server automatically
questions.explanation: Correct: A. On-premises file repositories require deployment of the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner, and for on-premises file shares DLP can move the file to a quarantine folder. B is wrong — on-premises locations need the scanner. C is wrong — on-premises repositories are a listed DLP location. D is wrong — endpoint DLP covers user devices, not the file server share.
questions.source_quote: On-premises file shares: move the file from where it's stored to a quarantine folder.

questions.question: A DLP policy is created with administrative units scoping so regional admins manage only their region's users. What is the effect of this scoping?
options: Administrative units expand an admin's scope to the whole tenant
Administrators assigned to an administrative unit can only create and manage policies for the users, groups, distribution groups, accounts, and sites assigned to that unit
Administrative units apply only to retention labels, not DLP
Scoping is ignored for Enterprise applications and devices policies
questions.explanation: Correct: B. DLP supports assigning Administrative Units to some Enterprise applications and devices policies, and admins assigned to a unit can only create and manage policies for the users, groups, distribution groups, accounts, and sites assigned to it. A reverses the effect. C is wrong — administrative scoping is a DLP policy configuration step. D is wrong — it applies to Enterprise applications and devices policies.
questions.source_quote: Administrators who are assigned to an administrative unit can only create and manage policies for the users, groups, distribution groups, accounts, and sites that they're assigned to.

questions.question: A user is about to email a spreadsheet with 200 customer bank account numbers to an external auditor. The DLP policy shows a pop-up tip warning them, and they can override with a justification. Which protective action is this, and where is the attempt recorded?
options: Audit only; the user sees no tip and nothing is recorded
Block without override; recorded only in the Exchange transport log
Block with override via policy tip; all DLP monitored activities are recorded to the Microsoft 365 Audit log by default and routed to Activity explorer
Quarantine; recorded only in the DLP alert queue
questions.explanation: Correct: C. DLP can show a pop-up policy tip warning the user, and block sharing while allowing override and capturing justification; all DLP monitored activities are recorded to the Microsoft 365 Audit log by default and routed to Activity explorer. B is wrong — block without override gives no override option. A is wrong — a tip is shown and activity is logged. D is wrong — quarantine applies to data at rest, not this email flow.
questions.source_quote: All DLP monitored activities are recorded to the Microsoft 365 Audit log by default and routed to Activity explorer.

questions.question: A multinational wants DLP to stop employees pasting sensitive data into ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek in the browser, and to cover unmanaged cloud apps on the network. Which DLP policy type covers this?
options: Enterprise applications and devices policies only
Retention policies, which block browser uploads
Endpoint DLP policies, which inspect all network traffic
Inline web traffic policies with collection policies, targeting data transmitted on the network and in Microsoft Edge for Business
questions.explanation: Correct: D. DLP with collection policies monitors and protects against oversharing to unmanaged cloud apps by targeting data transmitted on the network and in Microsoft Edge for Business, with Inline web traffic locations covering ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek. A is wrong — enterprise apps and devices policies cover Microsoft 365 locations and endpoints, not inline web traffic. C is wrong — endpoint DLP covers device actions, not network inline inspection. B is wrong — retention governs lifecycle, not exfiltration blocking.
questions.source_quote: DLP, with collection policies, monitors and protects against oversharing to Unmanaged cloud apps by targeting data transmitted on your network and in Microsoft Edge for Business.

questions.question: A document labeled Highly Confidential is downloaded from SharePoint by an authorized user, then emailed externally as an attachment. What protects it after download, and why?
options: The sensitivity label is persistent in the file metadata, so encryption and access restrictions travel with the content wherever it goes
Nothing; SharePoint permissions stop applying once a file is downloaded
Only the DLP policy tip travels with the file
The file is automatically deleted when it leaves SharePoint
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Sensitivity labels are persistent because the label is stored in metadata for files and emails, so the label stays with the content no matter where it is saved or stored, and encryption-based access control continues to restrict who can open it. B is wrong — label protection persists beyond SharePoint. C is wrong — policy tips are notifications, not protection. D is wrong — DLP does not delete files on download.
questions.source_quote: Persistent. Because the label is stored in metadata for files and emails, the label stays with the content, no matter where you save or store it.

questions.question: A company wants a Confidential label that encrypts documents, applies a Confidential watermark, and lets all employees modify the document while a specific external partner group can only view it. Is this possible with one label?
options: No, labels can only encrypt or watermark, never both
Yes, a label can apply encryption with per-user/group permissions and content markings such as headers, footers, and watermarks
No, external users can never be given permissions through a label
Yes, but only if the document stays in SharePoint and is never emailed
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Labels can control access using encryption, choosing which users or groups have permissions to perform which actions and for how long, and can mark content with watermarks, headers, or footers. A is wrong — encryption and markings are both label protection settings. C is wrong — the example explicitly allows a group in another organization view-only access. D is wrong — label protection travels with the content.
questions.source_quote: Provide protection settings that include encryption and content markings. For example, apply a Confidential label to a document or email, and that label encrypts the content and applies a Confidential watermark.

questions.question: An admin creates labels Public, General, Confidential, and Highly Confidential, and lists them in that order top to bottom in the portal. Users report that the most restrictive label is not treated as highest priority. What is wrong?
options: The order is correct; priority is alphabetical
Priority is set by the label color, not the list order
Label order sets priority: the most restrictive label, such as Highly Confidential, should appear at the bottom of the list, and the least restrictive at the top
All labels have equal priority by design
questions.explanation: Correct: C. The order of labels in the portal is important because it sets their priority: the most restrictive label should appear at the bottom of the list and the least restrictive at the top. A is wrong — priority is list order, not alphabetical. B is wrong — color does not set priority. D is wrong — priority order matters, e.g. for auto-labeling precedence.
questions.source_quote: You want your most restrictive sensitivity label, such as Highly Confidential, to appear at the bottom of the list, and your least restrictive sensitivity label, such as Personal or Public, to appear at the top.

questions.question: A Teams site for an M&A project must block external sharing, block access from unmanaged devices, and be non-discoverable as a private team. The site contains thousands of files that should not each be labeled individually. What is the right approach?
options: Create a retention label for the site, which controls external sharing
Label every file manually with the Files scope
Use a DLP policy on the Teams chat location, which controls site settings
Apply a sensitivity label with the Groups and sites scope to the container, which protects the container without labeling individual items
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Sensitivity labels for containers protect Teams sites, Microsoft 365 Groups, and SharePoint sites by controlling privacy, external access, external sharing, unmanaged device access, and private team discoverability, without labeling the items inside. B is wrong — container labeling exists precisely to avoid per-item labeling. C is wrong — DLP governs content movement, not container settings. A is wrong — retention labels govern lifecycle, not sharing controls.
questions.source_quote: Protect containers that include Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups, SharePoint sites. For example, set privacy settings, external user access and external sharing, access from unmanaged devices, and control how channels can be shared with other teams.

questions.question: A user applies a sensitivity label to an email, and the admin later discovers the label name is visible in clear text in the message metadata. Is this a misconfiguration?
options: No, labels are stored in clear text in metadata by design, so third-party apps and services can read them and apply their own protective actions
Yes, labels must be encrypted in metadata
Yes, but only for emails; file labels are encrypted
No, because the label is only visible to the sender
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Sensitivity labels are clear text in metadata by design: third-party apps and services can read the label and apply their own protective actions. B is wrong — clear text is intended. C is wrong — files and emails both store the label in clear-text metadata. D is wrong — the label is readable by services, not only the sender.
questions.source_quote: Clear text. Because the label is stored in clear text in the metadata for files and emails, third-party apps and services can read it and then apply their own protective actions, if required.

questions.question: A defense contractor must hold encryption keys within a geographical boundary and ensure that under all circumstances only the organization can decrypt its most sensitive documents. Which solution fits, and what is its key property?
options: Customer Key, because Microsoft never holds any key
Double Key Encryption, which uses two keys: one in the organization's control and a second stored securely in Azure, and viewing the data requires access to both keys
Standard sensitivity label encryption, which already guarantees only the organization can decrypt
BitLocker, which is the Purview mechanism for document keys
questions.explanation: Correct: B. DKE uses two keys to protect data — one key in your control and a second key stored securely in Microsoft Azure — and viewing data protected with DKE requires access to both keys; it is for organizations that must hold keys within a geographical boundary. A is wrong — Customer Key is a different service-encryption control. C is wrong — standard label encryption uses Microsoft-managed RMS keys. D is wrong — BitLocker is disk encryption, not Purview document protection.
questions.source_quote: It uses two keys to protect data; one key in your control and a second key you store securely in Microsoft Azure. Viewing data protected with Double Key Encryption requires access to both keys.

questions.question: A company applies DKE labels to its crown-jewel documents, then discovers users cannot co-author them, eDiscovery cannot search them, and Copilot cannot use them. What is the correct interpretation?
options: The DKE deployment is broken and must be reinstalled
DKE only works for emails, not documents
These are documented DKE limitations: DKE-encrypted content is not accessible to Microsoft 365 services including Copilot, and co-authoring, AutoSave, eDiscovery, and search do not work for DKE files
The users lack E5 licenses, which is the only cause
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Microsoft documents that DKE-encrypted data is not accessible at rest to Microsoft 365 services including Copilot, and that co-authoring and AutoSave are not supported, SharePoint/OneDrive cannot process DKE files, and eDiscovery, DLP, and search do not work for them. A is wrong — this is by design. B is wrong — DKE works for Office documents. D is wrong — licensing is E5, but the limitations apply regardless.
questions.source_quote: DKE encrypted data isn't accessible at rest to Microsoft 365 services including Copilot.

questions.question: A bank's most sensitive 5% of data is subject to strict key-custody rules, while 80% is nonsensitive and 15% is sensitive. How should DKE be scoped?
options: Apply DKE to all data for maximum protection
DKE must be applied tenant-wide or not at all
Apply DKE only to the nonsensitive 80%, since it is the largest set
Use Purview Information Protection with Microsoft-managed keys or bring-your-own-key for most data, and reserve DKE only for the mission-critical highly sensitive data
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Microsoft advises using Information Protection capabilities to protect most sensitive data and only using DKE for mission-critical data; DKE is not for every organization nor for all data. A is wrong — broad DKE would disable Copilot, eDiscovery, and co-authoring everywhere. C is backwards — DKE is for the most sensitive data. B is wrong — DKE is applied via labels to specific content.
questions.source_quote: Use Microsoft Purview Information Protection capabilities to protect most of your sensitive data and only use DKE for your mission-critical data.

questions.question: A DKE-protected document is stored in SharePoint. A user tries to open it in Office for the web. What happens, and what must they do instead?
options: SharePoint and OneDrive can't process DKE-encrypted files, so it can't be opened in Office for the web; the user must open it with a supported desktop application on their local computer
It opens normally in the browser with full co-authoring
It opens but the DKE protection is silently removed
It can be opened in the browser only if the user has a DKE viewer license
questions.explanation: Correct: A. SharePoint and OneDrive cannot process DKE-encrypted files: they cannot be opened in Office for the web, and collaborative features such as co-authoring, eDiscovery, DLP, and search do not work for them; protected content must be viewed using supported desktop applications. B is wrong — browser opening is unsupported. C is wrong — protection is never silently removed. D is wrong — there is no browser viewer license that enables this.
questions.source_quote: SharePoint and OneDrive can't process DKE-encrypted files. These files can't be opened in Office for the web.

questions.question: An app team stores database connection strings and API keys in application code. A security review flags this. What does Azure Key Vault guidance recommend instead?
options: Store secrets in environment variables on each VM, which is equivalent
Centralize application secrets in Key Vault and let apps retrieve specific versions by URI, so security information is no longer part of the code
Store secrets in a SharePoint list with restricted permissions
Encrypt the code repository, which protects secrets embedded in code
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Centralizing secrets in Key Vault lets apps retrieve what they need by URI, eliminates storing security information in applications, and greatly reduces accidental leakage. A is wrong — environment variables on VMs are still exposed in code-adjacent config. C is wrong — SharePoint is not a secrets store. D is wrong — encrypting the repo does not remove secrets from code or control their distribution.
questions.source_quote: Centralizing storage of application secrets in Azure Key Vault allows you to control their distribution. Key Vault greatly reduces the chances that secrets may be accidentally leaked.

questions.question: A regulated customer needs HSM-protected keys that never leave the HSM boundary, with FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validation. Which Key Vault tier meets this, and what does the Standard tier offer instead?
options: Standard tier, which offers HSM-protected keys
Either tier, because both use identical HSMs
Premium tier, which offers HSM-protected keys generated and protected by FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSMs; Standard encrypts with software libraries validated to FIPS 140 Level 1
Neither tier; Key Vault does not support HSMs
questions.explanation: Correct: C. The Premium tier offers HSM-protected keys generated and protected by FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSMs, while the Standard tier encrypts data using software libraries validated to FIPS 140 Level 1. A reverses the tiers. B is wrong — the tiers differ precisely on HSM protection. D is wrong — Premium HSM support is a headline feature.
questions.source_quote: Premium tier - Offers HSM-protected keys, generated and protected by FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated Marvell LiquidSecurity HSMs, for the highest level of cryptographic protection.

questions.question: A team must grant an application read access to one secret in one vault, and a DBA team management access to the vault itself. Which authorization models apply, and what is the key difference?
options: Key Vault access policy for both, because RBAC cannot manage vaults
Both models are identical and interchangeable
RBAC can only be used for data access, and access policy only for management
Azure RBAC can be used for both management of the vaults and access to data stored in a vault, while Key Vault access policy can only be used when accessing data stored in a vault
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Authentication is via Microsoft Entra ID; authorization may be done via Azure RBAC or Key Vault access policy, and RBAC can be used for both management of the vaults and data access, while access policy can only be used for data access. A is wrong — RBAC covers management too. C reverses the distinction. B is wrong — the scope difference is the point.
questions.source_quote: Azure RBAC can be used for both management of the vaults and to access data stored in a vault, while key vault access policy can only be used when attempting to access data stored in a vault.

questions.question: A company uses Key Vault for disk encryption keys, SQL Transparent Data Encryption, and App Service secrets. An auditor asks whether Microsoft can see or extract the stored data. What is the correct answer?
options: Azure Key Vault is designed so that Microsoft doesn't see or extract your data
Microsoft routinely extracts vault contents for support purposes
Microsoft can extract secrets but not keys
Only Premium tier vaults are hidden from Microsoft
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Microsoft states Azure Key Vault is designed so that Microsoft doesn't see or extract your data, and all vaults are encrypted at rest using keys stored in HSMs. B is wrong — no routine extraction occurs. C is wrong — the design covers keys, secrets, and certificates. D is wrong — the design applies to both tiers.
questions.source_quote: Finally, Azure Key Vault is designed so that Microsoft doesn't see or extract your data.

questions.question: A partner organization needs access to a SharePoint site and a SaaS app in your tenant, but has no IT department and no Microsoft Entra ID. How does B2B collaboration handle this?
options: It cannot; partners must have Microsoft Entra ID
The partner uses their own work, school, or social identities, or an email one-time passcode, and is represented in your directory as a guest user object
You must create a member account with a password you manage
You must sync their entire directory into yours
questions.explanation: Correct: B. With B2B, partners use their own identities and credentials whether or not they have a Microsoft Entra account, guests sign in with work, school, or social identities, and the email one-time passcode feature is on by default for new tenants. A is wrong — B2B explicitly works without the partner having Entra ID. C is wrong — no password management by the host is needed. D is wrong — no directory sync is required.
questions.source_title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
questions.source_quote: Work securely with external partners, even if they don't have Microsoft Entra ID or an IT department.

questions.question: A company allows B2B collaboration with Fabrikam in cross-tenant access settings, but then adds fabrikam.com to blocked domains in external collaboration settings. What happens to new invitations and existing guests?
options: New invitations are blocked and existing guests lose access immediately
The cross-tenant setting overrides, so new invitations still work
Users can't invite new Fabrikam guests, but existing Fabrikam guests can continue using B2B collaboration
Both settings are ignored and all guests are blocked
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Microsoft's example states that when Fabrikam is allowed in cross-tenant access but its domain is added to blocked domains, users cannot invite new Fabrikam business guests, but existing Fabrikam guests can continue using B2B collaboration — the most restrictive setting applies to new invitations. A is wrong — existing guests are unaffected. B is wrong — the most restrictive setting applies. D is wrong — neither setting is ignored.
questions.source_title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
questions.source_quote: Your users can't invite new Fabrikam business guests, but existing Fabrikam guests can continue using B2B collaboration.

questions.question: A security team wants guests from a trusted partner tenant to avoid re-registering MFA in the host tenant, but only for that one partner. Where is this configured, and what is the risk if applied broadly?
options: In external collaboration settings for all guests, with no risk
It cannot be configured per partner; it is tenant-wide only
In Conditional Access, by excluding all guests from MFA
In cross-tenant access organizational settings for that partner, trusting MFA claims from the partner tenant; trusting claims broadly without a security review weakens assurance
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Cross-tenant access settings let you create organization-specific settings and trust MFA and device claims from other Microsoft Entra organizations; the default is not to trust them, and trust should follow a security review. A is wrong — external collaboration settings do not control MFA trust. C is wrong — excluding guests from MFA removes protection. B is wrong — organizational settings are per-partner.
questions.source_title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
questions.source_quote: Using cross-tenant access settings, you can also trust multifactor (MFA) and device claims (compliant claims and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined claims) from other Microsoft Entra organizations.

questions.question: An admin is confused about which setting controls who can invite guests versus which external tenants can authenticate. What is the correct split?
options: External collaboration settings control which users in the organization are allowed to send B2B invitations; cross-tenant access settings control whether users can authenticate with external Microsoft Entra tenants
Cross-tenant access settings control who can send invitations; external collaboration settings control authentication
Both settings do the same thing and either can be used
Neither setting exists; invitations are controlled by Conditional Access only
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Cross-tenant access settings control whether users can authenticate with external Microsoft Entra tenants, while external collaboration settings control which users in the organization are allowed to send B2B collaboration invitations to guests from any organization. B reverses the split. C is wrong — they manage two different aspects. D is wrong — both settings exist in External Identities.
questions.source_title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
questions.source_quote: Cross-tenant access settings control whether users can authenticate with external Microsoft Entra tenants. By contrast, external collaboration settings control which users in your organization are allowed to send B2B collaboration invitations to guests from any organization.

questions.question: A European bank purchases Advanced Data Residency and wants to know what Microsoft commits to store at rest in the Local Region Geography for Purview DLP. What is in scope?
options: Only the DLP policy names, not the configuration
DLP Admin Configuration and DLP policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, among other listed customer data
All Microsoft 365 data automatically, with no service list
Only audit logs; DLP configuration is stored globally
questions.explanation: Correct: B. The ADR commitments list for Purview DLP includes DLP Admin Configuration and DLP policies in the Microsoft Purview portal as customer data stored at rest in the Local Region Geography. A is wrong — configuration is in scope. C is wrong — only listed services are covered. D is wrong — DLP configuration is explicitly listed.
questions.source_quote: This article lists the Data Residency commitments (available with the Advanced Data Residency add-on) for supported Microsoft Purview services and solutions.

questions.question: A compliance officer assumes Advanced Data Residency covers every Purview service automatically. What is the correct caveat?
options: ADR covers all Purview services with no exceptions
ADR applies only to Exchange, not Purview
The Purview services list includes all services covered as part of the ADR commitment as of February 2026, and additional Purview services aren't currently supported
ADR coverage is decided per user, not per service
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Microsoft states the Purview services list includes all services covered as part of the ADR commitment as of February 2026 and additional Microsoft Purview services are not currently supported. A is wrong — coverage is a defined list. B is wrong — Purview DLP and Information Protection are listed. D is wrong — coverage is per service.
questions.source_quote: The Microsoft Purview services list includes all services covered as part of the Advanced Data Residency commitment as of February 2026. Additional Microsoft Purview services aren't currently supported.

questions.question: A company wants DLP coverage for Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses so sensitive data is not pasted into Copilot. Which DLP location applies, and what is its status?
options: Copilot prompts are covered by Exchange DLP automatically
Copilot cannot be a DLP location under any circumstances
Copilot is covered only by sensitivity labels, never DLP
Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot chat is a DLP location (preview), alongside Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, devices, and Fabric/Power BI
questions.explanation: Correct: D. DLP locations include Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot chat (preview), in addition to Microsoft 365 services, Office apps, devices, non-Microsoft cloud apps, on-premises repositories, and Fabric/Power BI workspaces. B is wrong — Copilot is a listed location. C is wrong — DLP policies can target Copilot. A is wrong — Exchange covers mail, not Copilot interactions.
questions.source_quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot chat (preview).

questions.question: An employee shares a file containing passport numbers in a Teams private channel. The DLP policy covers Teams chat and channel messages. What does DLP do, and where is the file itself also protected?
options: DLP extends to Teams chat and channel messages including private channels, and files shared in Teams are stored in SharePoint/OneDrive so those locations also apply
DLP only covers public channels, so private channels are exempt
DLP blocks the message but the file is never scanned
Teams DLP requires a separate product and is not part of Purview
questions.explanation: Correct: A. DLP capabilities extend to Teams chat and channel messages, including messages in private channels, and files shared in Teams are stored in SharePoint and OneDrive, which are also DLP locations. B is wrong — private channels are covered. C is wrong — the file is scanned under SharePoint/OneDrive locations. D is wrong — Teams DLP is part of Purview DLP.
questions.source_title: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview
questions.source_quote: Data loss prevention capabilities extend to Microsoft Teams chat and channel messages, whether it's in a message or a file, including messages in private channels.

questions.question: A DLP rule uses Stop processing more rules and the policy is in simulation mode. An analyst expects later rules to be skipped during the simulation. What actually happens?
options: Later rules are skipped exactly as in enforce mode
Stop processing more rules doesn't work in simulation mode, even when it's turned on
Simulation mode processes rules in reverse order
The policy is automatically switched to enforce mode
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Microsoft notes that Stop processing more rules doesn't work in simulation mode, even when it's turned on — so simulation results may show matches from later rules that would be skipped in enforcement. A is wrong — the setting is ineffective in simulation. C is wrong — rule order does not reverse. D is wrong — simulation never auto-enforces.
questions.source_quote: Stop processing more rules doesn't work in simulation mode, even when it's turned on.

questions.question: A sensitivity label is configured for a Teams meeting with encryption. A guest from another organization joins. What is true about the guest and the label?
options: Guests can see and select your sensitivity labels in apps
The label is automatically removed when a guest joins
Users from other organizations or guests can't see your sensitivity labels in apps, but the meeting's label protection still applies to the meeting content
Guests must apply the label themselves before joining
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Microsoft states users from other organizations or guests cannot see your sensitivity labels in apps, while labels can protect meetings and chat by labeling and optionally encrypting meeting invites and enforcing Teams-specific options. A is wrong — guests cannot see the labels. B is wrong — labels are not removed by guest attendance. D is wrong — guests do not apply labels.
questions.source_quote: Users from other organizations or guests can't see your sensitivity labels in apps.

questions.question: A company enables sensitivity labels for SharePoint document libraries as the default label, and selects the option to extend protection for unencrypted files. A user downloads an unencrypted file from the library. What happens?
options: The file is deleted on download
The download is blocked entirely
The file loses all protection because it was unencrypted
When the file is downloaded, the current SharePoint permissions travel with the labeled file
questions.explanation: Correct: D. When you configure a default sensitivity label for SharePoint document libraries and select the option to extend protection for unencrypted files, then when these files are downloaded, the current SharePoint permissions travel with the labeled file. A is wrong — files are not deleted. C is wrong — the extension exists precisely to carry protection to downloaded files. B is wrong — downloads are allowed with protection.
questions.source_quote: Extend SharePoint protection when files are downloaded when you configure a default sensitivity label for SharePoint document libraries and select the option to extend protection for unencrypted files. Then, when these files are downloaded, the current SharePoint permissions travel with the labeled file.

questions.question: A user wants to label a document Public for identification only, with no encryption or markings, and add protection later if needed. Is this supported?
options: Yes, you can label content without using any protection settings, purely to identify sensitivity and generate usage reports, and apply protection later
No, every label must apply encryption
No, labels without protection are deleted after 24 hours
Yes, but only for emails, not documents
questions.explanation: Correct: A. You can apply a label as a result of identifying sensitivity without protection settings; this provides a visual mapping and generates usage reports, and you can always choose to apply protection settings later. B is wrong — protection settings are optional per label. C is wrong — no such deletion exists. D is wrong — it applies to files and emails.
questions.source_quote: You can also just apply a label as a result of identifying the sensitivity of the data. Based on this information, you can always choose to apply protection settings later.

questions.question: An admin creates a label scoped only to Groups and sites, then wonders why users cannot select it for a Word document. What is the cause?
options: The label is broken and must be recreated
Label scope determines which settings you can configure and whether users can see and select the label; a Groups and sites-only label can't be selected for items like files
Word does not support sensitivity labels at all
The label needs 24 hours before it appears in Word
questions.explanation: Correct: B. When you create a sensitivity label, you choose its scope, which determines which settings you can configure and the availability of the label to apps and services, including whether users can see and select it; labels just for groups and sites cannot be selected for items. A is wrong — the label works as designed. C is wrong — Word supports labels. D is wrong — scope, not timing, is the cause.
questions.source_quote: This scope configuration means you can have sensitivity labels that are just for items such as files, emails, and meetings, and can't be selected for groups and sites. Similarly, you can have sensitivity labels that are just for groups and sites and can't be selected for items.

questions.question: A company wants automatic labeling of files containing customer passport numbers, with a prompt to the user when confidence is lower. Which label capability provides this?
options: Manual labeling only; automatic labeling is not supported for files
DLP simulation mode, which labels files automatically
Auto-labeling: apply the label automatically to files and emails, or recommend a label with a policy tip prompt
Retention labels, which auto-apply sensitivity labels
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Labels can be applied automatically, or you can prompt users to apply the label you recommend by using a policy tip. A is wrong — auto-labeling for files and emails is supported. B is wrong — simulation mode does not label. D is wrong — retention labels govern lifecycle, not sensitivity auto-labeling.
questions.source_quote: Apply the label automatically to files and emails, or recommend a label. If you recommend a label, you can customize the prompt.

questions.question: A firm uses Microsoft 365 Copilot and wants labeled data to stay protected when Copilot processes it. What do sensitivity labels do here, and what is the DKE exception?
options: Labels are ignored by Copilot entirely
Only DKE labels work with Copilot; standard labels are ignored
Copilot strips labels before processing
Copilot and agents recognize and integrate sensitivity labels to help keep labeled data protected, but DKE-encrypted data isn't accessible to Copilot
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Copilot and agents recognize and integrate sensitivity labels into user interactions to help keep labeled data protected, while DKE-encrypted data is not accessible at rest to Microsoft 365 services including Copilot. A is wrong — Copilot integrates labels. C is wrong — Copilot does not strip labels. B reverses the exception — DKE is the case Copilot cannot use.
questions.source_quote: Copilot and agents recognize and integrate sensitivity labels into the user interactions to help keep labeled data protected.

questions.question: A company with an on-premises key management server wants DKE so encrypted data remains opaque wherever it is stored, and keys stay in the same geography as the data. Is this deployment supported?
options: Yes, DKE supports cloud and on-premises deployments, you can host the DKE service in a location of your choice, and you can store data and key in the same geographical location
No, DKE requires keys to be stored in Microsoft's datacenters
Yes, but only if the data is also stored on-premises
No, DKE only works with Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
questions.explanation: Correct: A. DKE supports several configurations including both cloud and on-premises deployments, you can host the DKE service in a location of your choice, and DKE gives you the control to store your data and key in the same geographical location. B is wrong — one key stays in your control. C is wrong — data can be stored on-premises or moved to the cloud. D is wrong — DKE uses its own service, not only Managed HSM.
questions.source_quote: You can host the Double Key Encryption service used to request your key in a location of your choice. Double Key Encryption gives you the control to store your data and key in the same geographical location.

questions.question: A DKE label is applied to a document and a user tries to use Encrypt Only and Do Not Forward in Outlook on the same message. What happens?
options: Both work normally with DKE
Encrypt Only and Do Not Forward aren't supported with DKE in Outlook, though all other Office applications support user-defined permission labels with DKE
Do Not Forward works but Encrypt Only does not
Outlook does not support DKE at all
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Encrypt Only and Do Not Forward are not supported with DKE in Outlook; all other Office applications support user-defined permission labels with DKE. A is wrong — the Outlook exception is documented. C is wrong — both are unsupported in Outlook with DKE. D is wrong — Outlook supports DKE labels generally.
questions.source_quote: Encrypt Only and Do Not Forward aren't supported with DKE in Outlook. All other Office applications support user-defined permission labels with DKE.

questions.question: A Key Vault admin wants to audit who accessed which secret and when, and to archive those logs long-term. What does Key Vault support?
options: Key Vault has no logging capability
Logs are only available in the Premium tier
Enable logging for vaults: archive to a storage account, stream to an event hub, or send logs to Azure Monitor logs
Logs are automatically sent to Microsoft and cannot be accessed by the customer
questions.explanation: Correct: C. You can monitor Key Vault activity by enabling logging: archive to a storage account, stream to an event hub, or send logs to Azure Monitor logs, and you control the logs including restricting access. A is wrong — logging is supported. B is wrong — logging is not tier-gated. D is wrong — the customer controls the logs.
questions.source_quote: You can configure Azure Key Vault to archive to a storage account, stream to an event hub, or send the logs to Azure Monitor logs.

questions.question: A company creates one Key Vault per application so each app's secrets are segregated. An auditor asks whether this is supported and what it achieves. What is the answer?
options: Not supported; one vault per tenant is the limit
Not supported; secrets must be stored in a single central vault
Supported, but all vaults share the same access policy
Supported: Key Vaults allow you to segregate application secrets, and applications may access only the vault they are allowed to access and only perform specific operations
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Key Vaults allow segregating application secrets: you can create a Key Vault per application and restrict the secrets stored in it to a specific application and team, with applications limited to specific operations. A is wrong — there is no one-vault-per-tenant limit. C is wrong — access is per vault. B is wrong — per-application vaults are the recommended segregation pattern.
questions.source_quote: You can create an Azure Key Vault per application and restrict the secrets stored in a Key Vault to a specific application and team of developers.

questions.question: A guest user is invited to collaborate, redeems the invitation, and appears in the directory. How is this guest represented, and what does their user principal name contain?
options: As a user object with user type typically set to guest and a UPN containing the #EXT# identifier
As a member user with a standard UPN
As a service principal with no UPN
Guests are not represented as directory objects at all
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Once the guest redeems the invitation or completes sign-up, they are represented in the directory as a user object, the user type is typically set to guest, and their UPN contains the #EXT# identifier. B is wrong — guests are guest type, not member. C is wrong — guests are user objects, not service principals. D is wrong — guests are directory objects.
questions.source_title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
questions.source_quote: Once the guest redeems their invitation or completes sign-up, they're represented in your directory as a user object. The user type for these B2B collaboration users is typically set to guest and their user principal name contains the #EXT# identifier.

questions.question: A company shares a SharePoint folder with an external auditor who has no corporate identity. The auditor will authenticate via an email one-time passcode. What must be true about the sharing setup?
options: SharePoint sharing with external users requires a separate product
When enabling integration with SharePoint and OneDrive, you also enable the email one-time passcode feature in B2B to serve as a fallback authentication method
One-time passcodes cannot be used for SharePoint sharing
The auditor must be given a member account first
questions.explanation: Correct: B. When enabling integration with SharePoint and OneDrive, you also enable the email one-time passcode feature in Microsoft Entra B2B to serve as a fallback authentication method, and the feature is on by default for new tenants. A is wrong — SharePoint/OneDrive integration with B2B is built in. C is wrong — OTP is the fallback method. D is wrong — guests authenticate with their own identity or OTP.
questions.source_title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
questions.source_quote: When enabling integration with SharePoint and OneDrive, you also enable the email one-time passcode feature in Microsoft Entra B2B to serve as a fallback authentication method.

questions.question: A DLP policy covers Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and endpoint devices. A user copies a file with health records to a personal Dropbox account from their managed laptop. Which DLP coverage applies?
options: None, because Dropbox is not a Microsoft service
Only the Exchange location, because the file was once emailed
Endpoint DLP on the device, which can audit or restrict copying sensitive items to cloud sync destinations, and non-Microsoft cloud apps are a DLP location via Defender for Cloud Apps
Only retention labels apply to Dropbox uploads
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Endpoint DLP covers devices and can restrict copying sensitive items to removable or cloud destinations, and non-Microsoft cloud apps are a DLP location (Defender for Cloud Apps instances). A is wrong — DLP explicitly covers non-Microsoft cloud apps. B is wrong — Exchange covers mail, not endpoint uploads. D is wrong — retention does not block uploads.
questions.source_quote: DLP monitors and protects against oversharing in enterprise apps and on devices. It targets Microsoft 365 locations, like Exchange and SharePoint, and locations you add, like on-premises file shares, endpoint devices, and non-Microsoft cloud apps.

questions.question: A security team wants to protect data in third-party apps such as Salesforce, Box, and Dropbox even though those apps do not read sensitivity labels. Which capability does this?
options: Nothing; labels only work in Microsoft apps
Azure Policy, which enforces labels in Salesforce directly
Endpoint DLP, which relabels files inside third-party clouds
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, which can detect, classify, label, and protect content in third-party apps and services even if the app doesn't read or support sensitivity labels
questions.explanation: Correct: D. With Defender for Cloud Apps, you can detect, classify, label, and protect content in third-party apps and services such as Salesforce, Box, or Dropbox, even if the third-party app does not read or support sensitivity labels. A is wrong — the integration exists for this purpose. C is wrong — endpoint DLP covers devices, not third-party clouds. B is wrong — Azure Policy does not enforce labels inside Salesforce.
questions.source_quote: With Defender for Cloud Apps, you can detect, classify, label, and protect content in third-party apps and services, such as SalesForce, Box, or DropBox, even if the third-party app or service doesn't read or support sensitivity labels.

questions.question: A company in a regulated industry needs to keep encryption keys for its most sensitive data in its own datacenter, and all keys used for encryption and decryption maintained there. Which DKE requirement does this match?
options: DKE fits organizations with regulatory requirements to hold keys within a geographical boundary, and where all keys held for encryption and decryption are maintained in the organization's data center
No requirement; DKE keys are always held by Microsoft
This matches Customer Key, not DKE
This matches standard label encryption, which keeps keys on-premises
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Microsoft lists these exact requirements for DKE: regulatory requirements to hold keys within a geographical boundary, and all keys held for data encryption and decryption maintained in the organization's data center. B is wrong — DKE keeps one key in the organization's control. C is wrong — the quoted requirements are from the DKE page. D is wrong — standard label encryption uses Microsoft-managed RMS keys.
questions.source_quote: You have regulatory requirements to hold keys within a geographical boundary. All of the keys that you hold for data encryption and decryption are maintained in your data center.

questions.question: A DLP policy is turned on at 09:00. At 09:30 a user shares a sensitive file externally and it is not blocked. At 11:00 the same action is blocked. What most likely explains the delay?
options: DLP policies are evaluated only once a day at midnight
In general, policies take effect about an hour after being turned on
The policy was in simulation mode until 11:00 automatically
DLP only enforces after the first audit log export
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Microsoft notes that in general, policies take effect about an hour after being turned on. A is wrong — the delay is about an hour, not a daily cycle. C is wrong — simulation mode does not auto-switch to enforce. D is wrong — enforcement does not depend on log export.
questions.source_quote: In general, policies take effect about an hour after being turned on.
